# 2 Baruch Chapter 44 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 44 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 44:5 — "proud / proud ones"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-proud-ones" | Preserves the Syriac noun/adjective as a designation |
| LOGOS | "the proud" | Standard English substantive adjective |
| PNEUMA | "the proud" | Same |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA "the proud." Natural English.

**Status:** Consensus with minor variation.

---

## 44:7 — "great worth and great excellence / great worth and great greatness"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "things-of-great-worth and-great-greatness" | Syriac has two terms: worth + greatness |
| LOGOS | "of great worth and great excellence" | "Excellence" for the second term |
| PNEUMA | "of immense value and greatness" | "Immense" and "greatness" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "great worth and great excellence." Two Syriac terms are preserved as a pair. "Excellence" is a more varied English synonym than EMET's repeated "great-greatness."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 44:8 — "people of knowledge / people who truly know God"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "people-of-knowledge" | Literal: Syriac 'ida'ta = knowledge |
| LOGOS | "people of knowledge" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "people who truly know God" | Interprets "knowledge" as knowledge of God |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained LOGOS "people of knowledge." The Syriac 'ida'ta is the noun "knowledge/knowing" and does not explicitly specify God as the object. PNEUMA's reading is possible but adds specificity not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 44:10-11 — rhetorical questions

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Declarative interrogatives with "And-the-lamp-of-this-world" | Preserves Syriac structure |
| LOGOS | "this lamp of the world — how long will it shine?" | Fronts the topic |
| PNEUMA | "But how long will this world's lamp burn?" | Reverses and modernizes |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS structure. Fronting the lamp topic is more natural while preserving the Syriac topicalization. PNEUMA's reversal changes the rhetorical structure.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
